name: chawan
desc: TUI web browser with CSS, inline image and JavaScript support
why: A terminal web browser with CSS and inline images, an unusual take on a familiar thing.

brief.what_it_is: Chawan is a terminal web browser (TUI) with its own browser engine, written from scratch, that renders HTML with CSS, inline images (Sixel or Kitty protocol), and optional JavaScript. Input is a URL or local file, and output is a rendered page in the terminal. It also supports (S)FTP, Gopher, Gemini, Finger and Spartan, and it can be used as a terminal pager. The executables are cha (the browser) and mancha (a man page viewer).
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit problem statement. It says w3m was the main inspiration, and the project aims to display many websites in a manner similar to major graphical browsers, from inside a terminal.
brief.how_it_works: The README says Chawan uses its own small browser engine developed from scratch, rather than shared code with w3m. It runs as multi-processing with incremental loading of documents, and it applies syscall filter sandboxing on FreeBSD, OpenBSD and Linux (capsicum, pledge and seccomp-bpf). Its layout engine supports flow, table and flexbox layout, and CJK double-width characters.

brief.install_notes: Requires a Unix-like OS; Windows needs WSL. You must install the Nim compiler, version 2.0.0 or newer, ideally 2.2.12; 1.6.14 onward may work but is not recommended. Dependencies are OpenSSL (or LibreSSL), libssh2, brotli, pkg-config and GNU make (gmake on non-GNU systems). Clone the repo, run make, then make install. Packages exist for Alpine, Arch, Debian testing, FreeBSD, Gentoo (guru), Guix, Homebrew, NetBSD (pkgsrc-wip), NixOS, Slackware, Void, and an AUR chawan-git package. JavaScript is disabled by default, and inline images need enabling per doc/image.md.
brief.standout: The browser engine is written from scratch in Nim rather than reusing an existing engine, yet the project claims it renders many sites similarly to graphical browsers. It also doubles as a pager and a man page viewer (mancha) and supports several non-web protocols alongside HTTP(S).
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage feed shows a commit (e58406c, select: check if builder is valid on item addition) pushed by ~bptato about 2 hours before the snapshot, and a mailing list reply from about 2 hours earlier. No release date was visible on the page.
brief.caveats: No native Windows support; WSL is required. Building needs Nim 2.0 or newer, and 32-bit systems may need Nim 2.2 or newer or the -fpermissive CFLAGS workaround. JavaScript and inline images are disabled by default. The README says static binaries from releases may have outdated dependencies, and it lists 'a lot more planned' features. The README also asks that tickets and patches not be generated with artificial neural networks.
